conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced turned up; the evidence is peer and macro proxies (Fed hike on 2026-09-16, peers' deposit costs turning up, a 10y near 5.1-5.3% hitting AOCI and mortgage fees, a New England peer's new office NPL), partly offset by peers beating Q3 EPS and a full quarter of the hedge roll-off, so impact_sum is -0.9 and the scaled number is a mild lean (p_up 46) on an abs move of 5.5% set above the 3.56% historical median because the last three prints moved 8-17%.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS about $0.86-0.87: Benzinga quote page (updated 2026-10-13, $0.87, revenue $62.5M) https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WASH/earnings-forecasts and Tickflow ($0.86, revenue $62M) https://tickflow.io/stock/WASH/forecast, both read as search snippets only (Benzinga page returned 403). Company guide: NIM about 2.75% in Q3 and 2.80% in Q4, Q3 expenses just under $39M, tax rate about 21.5%, mid-single-digit loan growth (Q2 call transcript https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904). My own arithmetic from that guide (NII ~$42.5M, fees ~$18.3M, expenses ~$38.9M, provision ~$1.5M, 21.5% tax, ~19.2M diluted shares) gives about $0.83-0.84, i.e. about 2-3% under the bar, which is an inference, not a document.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.3M shares, 6.6% of float, 6.8 days to cover (Equibles page dated 2026-08-21, https://equibles.com/stocks/WASH); Benzinga early August 6.3% of float and declining (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WASH/short-interest). No October settlement found. Elevated days to cover for a bank but not a crowded short in the 18-23% sense. Options: the baseline chain is unusable (ATM spread 187% of mid, total OI 39), so there is no skew and no option-implied move; a third-party page quotes +/-8.9% implied (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/WASH/earnings) but off that same unusable chain. Sell side: KBW Hold $36 (2026-07-21), Piper Sandler Hold $35, Seaport downgrade to Neutral 2026-07-22 (https://www.investing.com/equities/washington-trust); spot $36.91 sits at or above most targets. Run-up: -5.75% over 20 days, -1.0% over 5, 8.3% off the 52-week high.

findings.finding: The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and the two New England peers that have reported Q3 2026 show deposit costs turning up (Independent Bank Corp total cost of deposits +6bp QoQ to 1.42%, core NIM flat at 3.76%; Citizens deposit costs +3bp to 1.66%), which puts WASH's Q4 NIM guide of 2.80% (given on 2026-07-20, when rates were still expected to be steady to lower) at risk for a bank funded with CDs and $456M of FHLB advances and only a 'little bit left' of CD repricing down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (NIM +10bp to 2.73% with a 2.75%/2.80% guide) moved +8.15% over the window; Q1 2026 -16.9% was on credit, not margin. NIM direction has been the positive line for WASH through 2025-26 as rates fell.
findings.why_not_priced: WASH has not spoken since 2026-07-20; the 2.80% Q4 guide predates the September hike and the late-September 10y spike to 5.1-5.3%. If the market had priced a guide cut, consensus would sit below the $0.86-0.87 shown on 2026-10-13 and the stock would not be at or above the sell-side targets; the -5.75% 20-day move is in line with small caps (-7.2% in Q3) rather than name-specific.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. Second source: Citizens Q3 2026 release, deposit costs +3bp, NIM +2bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000759944/000075994426000206/a3q26earningsrelease.htm); Fed hike reported at https://forexfundamentals.com/economic-calendar/fomc/2026-09-16 (secondary, not the Fed statement).

findings.finding: WASH carried $982M amortized cost / $885M fair value of AFS securities with $100M of gross unrealized losses at 2026-06-30 (10-Q); with the 10y rising from about 4.45% in mid-June to 5.1-5.3% in late September, the Q3 AOCI hit is likely in the $25-40M pre-tax range, cutting tangible book from $25.46 by roughly 4-6% and TCE from 7.49% toward 7%; peers show the same mechanism (Citizens TBV -6.6% QoQ on higher long rates, INDB $78.4M AFS loss through OCI).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No WASH print in the baseline turned on AOCI; 2022-23 rate spikes hit TBV but the baseline only covers 2025-26.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the rate move and peers' TBV hits are public and computable. What is not in the wire is WASH's own TBV number; at 1.45x TBV a 5% TBV cut is noticed by bank investors who screen on P/TBV. If fully priced, the stock would have fallen more than small caps in late September; it did not visibly.
findings.independence: Company document (10-Q AFS table) plus peer releases: Citizens https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000759944/000075994426000206/a3q26earningsrelease.htm, rate level https://statisticsoftheworld.com/news/2026-09-23. Shares the rate driver with the NIM finding but lands on a different line (book value, not earnings).

findings.finding: New England office CRE stress continued into Q3 2026: Independent Bank Corp moved one office loan to nonperforming (NPLs $103.6M to $125.7M) and took a $6.5M provision mostly as a specific reserve on it; WASH carries $212.1M of office CRE with $31.7M special mention and $35.0M classified (of which $28.9M nonaccrual) at 2026-06-30, and an analyst flagged a $3.8M special-mention Class B office loan maturing in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit is the line this stock has traded on hardest: Q1 2026 non-accrual jump -16.9%; Q2 2026 stable nonaccruals (78bp) and a lower provision +8.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: WASH's office book composition is in its own Q2 release, but the peer read-through (INDB, 2026-10-15) landed after WASH last spoke; no foreclosure, receivership or court record naming WASH turned up, so this is a tail, not a known loss. If the market expected a second credit leg, the stock would not be within 8% of its 52-week high and above most sell-side targets.
findings.independence: Peer document: https://finviz.com/news/403305/independent-bank-corp-reports-third-quarter-net-income-of-897-million (proxy, different bank). The $3.8M maturing loan is from the Q2 call transcript https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904, where management said 'We feel comfortable about where this is and where it's going to go', which argues against the finding and is why it is small. Counterpoint: Citizens' commercial CRE nonaccruals fell 18% YoY.

findings.finding: Fee income likely slips from Q2's $18.7M: Q2 wealth revenue ($11.2M) included $265K of seasonal tax fees that do not recur, Q3 markets were mixed (S&P 500 +2.3%, small caps -7.2%, bonds down) so AUA growth from the record $7.92B is likely small (INDB AUA +0.4% QoQ), and mortgage banking ($3.5M in Q2) faces 30-year rates near 6.8-7.45% (INDB mortgage income -20.7%, Citizens mortgage fees -17%); with the guided NIM and expenses this leaves EPS around $0.83-0.84 against a $0.86-0.87 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat ($0.83 against $0.77-0.79) on NII and fees moved +8.15%; Q1 2026 miss ($0.66 against $0.77) moved -16.9% but on credit.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sell side models fees off the same index levels. The $265K seasonal item and the mortgage drop seen at peers after 2026-10-15 may not be fully in a $0.87 estimate set before the peers reported; if it were, the Benzinga consensus would have drifted below Q2's run-rate-plus-hedge level rather than sitting at $0.87.
findings.independence: Peer documents: INDB https://finviz.com/news/403305/independent-bank-corp-reports-third-quarter-net-income-of-897-million and Citizens https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000759944/000075994426000206/a3q26earningsrelease.htm (Citizens wealth fees were +7%, which argues the other way on wealth). The EPS arithmetic is my inference from the WASH Q2 release and call, not a document.

findings.finding: Q3 is the first full quarter with no amortization of the terminated cash-flow-hedge loss (fully amortized 2026-05-01): management quantified about $0.7M of NII / 4bp of NIM over Q2, alongside deposits +3.8% QoQ, FHLB advances down $120M and loan-to-deposit 95.1% at 2026-06-30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The hedge roll-off drove the Q2 NIM +10bp that moved +8.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the 2.75% Q3 guide, so mostly priced; it is filed because it is the main offset to the negative funding-cost findings within the reported quarter.
findings.independence: Same fact in the company's Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000737468/000073746826000109/exhibit9912026q2.htm (one fact, one finding).

findings.finding: WASH filed a $150M universal shelf S-3 on 2026-08-07 (effective 2026-08-14) covering common, preferred and senior or subordinated debt, with no stated use of proceeds; it reads as a renewal of the 2023 shelf (File No. 333-274430) rather than a planned raise, and CET1 was 11.89% at June 30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on financing.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: nothing stated, no corroborated ramp or capital need; a routine shelf renewal on a well-capitalised bank, so signed at zero. It would matter only if the release paired a TCE drop (AOCI) with a sub-debt issue, which nothing indicates.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list shows no 8-K since 2026-07-20 and only a 0.9-share Form 4 sale by the CEO on 2026-07-28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737468/000073746826000111/primary_01.xml).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WASH beat in Q2 2026 and rose 8.15%; 3 of 7 prior prints up.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer beats are public, but WASH's consensus at $0.87 was set by 2026-10-13, before INDB (10-15) and Citizens (10-16) reported; if the market had read a sector-wide beat into WASH, the stock would not be down 1% over five days.

findings.finding: Positioning: about 6.6% of float short with 6.8 days to cover on roughly 113K shares a day (August data), a stock trading at or above most sell-side targets on Hold ratings, and a 20-day run-up of -5.75%; a clean credit line on 2026-10-19 meets a short book that needs a week to cover, which is the mechanism behind the +8.15% after Q2.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with; the mild negative lean sits with a -5.75% 20-day run-up that mostly tracks small caps, and against a stock at or above most sell-side targets, so the findings neither ride nor fight a priced view.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (proxy, macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company): Fed-hike / peer deposit-cost NIM finding shrunk from -0.8 to -0.6.

Lessons 3 and 5 (own caveat: management said it was comfortable on the maturing office loan, and the read-through is another bank's loan) plus the pessimism artefact: office-credit finding shrunk from -0.7 to -0.5.
Fee-income finding sized -0.5 to -0.4 because the EPS gap rests on my own arithmetic and Citizens' wealth fees went the other way.
Lesson 8 and the core's understatement note: abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 5.5 given the last three prints moved 8-17%; p_up moved 45 to 46 for proxy-only evidence.

Lessons 4, 6 and 7 left standing: the financing finding was already signed at zero after asking what the money buys, the bar has two roughly agreeing estimate sources plus a company NIM/expense guide, and short interest (6.6%, 6.8 days) was already checked and is not crowded.
